saml.description: SAML NameID format 'Transient' generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Different downstream identifiers across repeated logins are expected and should not be flagged as identity instability.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to an existing account if the email matches.
saml.note: An SSO login resolving to an existing user by verified email can be intended account linking rather than unintended principal collapse.

saml.description: SAML NameID defaults to Persistent and uses the Logto user ID as the NameID.
saml.note: An SP observing a stable opaque user ID instead of email/username is expected.

saml.description: When no resource is specified in authentication, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests that decode access tokens as JWTs will fail for non-security reasons unless a resource or organization token was requested.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session, which has a fixed 14-day TTL.
saml.note: Expiry earlier than configured refresh-token TTL is expected in this mode and is not a freshness bug.

saml.description: After signing key rotation, the previous key remains valid for existing tokens until it is removed.
saml.note: Acceptance of tokens signed by the previous key immediately after rotation is documented behavior.

saml.constraint: Logto SAML app documentation only describes Logto acting as a SAML Identity Provider for SP-initiated SAML applications. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML IdP-broker tests such as forged SAMLResponse-to-broker attacks against Logto in this protocol profile; the documented SAML surface is the SP-facing application endpoint, not an upstream SAML connector validation API.

For SAML tests, the flow is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST start from the service provider side and preserve RelayState/request correlation; IdP-initiated assumptions are invalid because Logto states IdP-initiated flow is not yet supported for SAML apps.

When testing identity binding for SAML apps, NameID format materially changes the downstream identifier semantics. Persistent and Unspecified use the Logto user ID; Email address uses the user's email; Transient generates a one-time identifier that changes on each authentication request. Do NOT treat Transient NameID changes across logins as an I4 collision/merge bug; they are by design.

For SAML email-binding collision and cross-login identity tests, account linking behavior is email-based for enterprise SSO connectors: SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. A SAML/SSO login that lands on an existing account by matching verified email may be by design, not an I4 violation. Distinguish email-linking behavior from unintended principal collapse.

For OIDC token-exchange tests used after SAML-related authentication, token exchange is disabled by default per application. The fuzzer MUST enable 'Allow token exchange' on the target application before expecting /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange to succeed.

For I5 token-exchange audience-binding tests, use the token endpoint parameter named 'resource' as the audience/resource indicator. The exchanged token is documented as bound to the specified resource. Tests must vary resource explicitly and verify the resulting token audience rather than assuming a separate 'audience' parameter name in Logto docs.

For I2 freshness tests on OIDC tokens obtained in SAML-adjacent flows, include a control exchange/login using a valid token and then call /oidc/me. Without a successful control, a failed attack case cannot be distinguished from missing scopes, wrong client configuration, or opaque-token handling differences.

If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume JWT structure for session_token in verify_granted_identity or token-exchange follow-up tests unless a resource/organization context was requested. Use /oidc/me for identity inspection, and use introspection only when separately configured with client authentication.

Refresh-token/session lifetime semantics have a sentinel-like interaction: a refresh token issued without offline_access is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Never assume the configured refresh-token TTL alone controls lifetime; include offline_access when testing long-lived token behavior.

Wildcard matching is documented for redirect URIs only, not for identity or authorization scope constraints. Do NOT infer wildcard support for subject, email, NameID, or claim matching from redirect URI behavior. For multi-identity I4 tests, treat undocumented identity constraint fields as exact-match-only unless explicitly documented otherwise.

For third-party/OIDC consent and scope tests that may be chained with SAML-origin sessions, non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently omitted' when interpreting I5 results.

Logto SAML applications support SP-initiated authentication flow only in the provided documentation. Do NOT attempt IdP-initiated SAML tests for this profile; failures there are not evidence of an invariant violation.

The provided documentation does NOT expose a concrete SAML ACS/callback HTTP path for SAML app login. Treat saml_login endpoint path as undocumented/absent unless discovered from runtime metadata or other docs; do NOT assume a guessed callback URL for security conclusions.

For SAML principal-binding tests, Name ID format materially changes the downstream identifier. Logto supports Persistent and Unspecified using Logto user ID, Email address using the user's email, and Transient using a one-time user ID that changes each authentication request. For I4 collision tests, do NOT use Transient because identity instability is by design; choose Persistent or Email address depending on the binding under test.

For SAML email-binding collision tests, Logto enterprise/SSO documentation states SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. A SAML/SSO login that merges into an existing account by matching verified email may be by design rather than an I4 bug. Distinguish email-based account linking from unintended NameID collisions.

For I5 scope/claim tests using /oidc/me, returned claims are scope-gated. Standard claims depend solely on requested OIDC scopes, while extended claims require BOTH the corresponding scope and an admin console toggle. Missing claims in /oidc/me or tokens are not authorization-binding failures unless both prerequisites were satisfied.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, enable the application's 'Allow token exchange' setting; otherwise rejection is expected and not evidence of correct audience/scope enforcement.

For token exchange audience-binding tests, use the token endpoint /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and set the target audience via the resource parameter. Do NOT interpret acceptance without a resource/audience target as an audience-binding bypass because the request did not ask for audience restriction.

Refresh token/session lifetime has a documented sentinel interaction: a refresh token issued WITHOUT offline_access is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Never assume the configured refresh token TTL alone controls validity; include offline_access when testing long-lived token behavior.

Rotate refresh token is effectively always-on for public clients when enabled: SPA/native clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh. Reuse of an old rotated refresh token may fail by design. Freshness/replay tests must track the newest refresh token returned after each refresh.

Wildcard matching is documented for redirect URIs only, not for SAML identifiers, NameID formats, scopes, or other auth-binding parameters in the provided SAML docs. Do NOT use '*' as a wildcard for identity-binding tests on SAML fields; absent explicit matching-mode documentation, treat such fields as exact or UI-configured only.

For I3 config-change tests involving signing key rotation, Logto documents that existing tokens signed by a previous key remain valid until the previous key is removed, and consecutive rotations may invalidate all issued tokens. Do NOT flag acceptance of old tokens immediately after one rotation as stale-cache unless the previous key has been removed or the test specifically targets new issuance behavior.

For OIDC verification after SAML-related flows, if no resource is specified Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. Use /oidc/me for identity verification, and use /oidc/token/introspection only with client authentication if token format inspection is required. Do NOT treat opaque-token format as a bug.

Logto SAML app documentation describes Logto as the Identity Provider (IdP) and your application as the Service Provider (SP). For target protocol saml, the broker under test consumes AuthnRequest and emits SAML assertions; it does NOT expose a documented upstream SAML assertion-consumption API in the provided docs. Do NOT run upstream-SAML broker attack patterns (e.g. saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_no_conditions, saml_wrong_audience) against Logto from this documentation set, because that would test the SP application, not Logto.

Only SP-initiated SAML flow is currently supported for SAML apps in the provided docs. IdP-initiated flow is explicitly future work. Tests must initiate authentication from the SP side and MUST NOT treat lack of IdP-initiated support as a flow-coherence or auth bypass bug.

NameID format is configurable and defaults to Persistent, which uses the Logto user ID as NameID. For I4 identity-binding tests, do NOT assume the downstream SP-visible identifier equals email or username unless the SAML app is explicitly configured to Email address format. A mismatch between sent email and observed NameID can be by design.

Transient NameID format generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request. When testing I4 cross-login identity stability or collision, do NOT use Transient NameID format because per-login identifier changes are by design and will create false positives.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 cross-protocol or SAML-email-binding collision tests involving enterprise SSO, email-based account linking is documented behavior and must not be flagged as an identity-collapse bug unless the resulting account merge exceeds the documented email-match rule.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced and saved as primary_email. For I4 tests that compare SSO-provided email against local account identity, ensure the upstream email is verified; otherwise absence of email binding is expected and not a bug.

Logto supports assertion signing and optional assertion encryption for SAML apps, but the provided docs do not document default signature-validation, issuer-validation, audience-validation, Conditions-validation, or replay-detection behavior at an HTTP API level. The fuzzer MUST NOT infer secure or insecure defaults for these checks from configuration prose alone; any result requires separate protocol-level observation and should not be treated as documentation-backed expected behavior.

SAML apps are limited in OSS: the open-source version supports only 3 SAML apps. Test harnesses that create per-test SAML applications must aggressively clean up or reuse applications to avoid setup failures unrelated to security.
